text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Rescuers follow burning stick: Helicopter crew members save 4 who swam to land after crash in icy North Atlantic.
- Zaire mission costly for Canada: Young estimates $100-million tab.
- Ottawa denies Krever key data: Documents to be kept from public.
- UN approval of rescue force 'close': Mandate for up to 12,000 troops does not include disarming Hutu militias.
- Quebec judge denied FLQ link, minister says: Therrien told Quebec cabinet to ignore rumours, said only his sister was involved with terrorists.
- Bank of Canada Governor hints at more rate cuts: Borrowing costs could drop further if inflation falls below 1 percent, Thiessen says.
- Richard Thomson stepping down as TD boss: Veteran CEO of Canada's fifth-largest bank handing helm to chief lieutenant Charles Baillie next year.
- Canada, Chile strike trade deal: Push now expected for expansion of NAFTA umbrella.
- Natural gas prices surge in Alberta: Winter's grip cuts storage levels.
- Home resales hit the roof: October sales jump 37 percent from last year to a new monthly record as consumers rush to take advantage of low interest rates, economists say.
- Crown Life offers US$27 million to settle suit.
